decision: Model the invoke-grant as an ordinary row in the existing choros.grant table (operation='invoke', resource_type='agent', lattice scope over the org hierarchy, target role carried in resource_facet.agent_role_id) with NO new authority subsystem. Two new HTTP routes POST /api/invoke/request (propose) and POST /api/invoke/command (execute-stub) read the caller from X-Dev-User, resolve the target agent's assigned role from agent_card + role_assignment, and decide via the SAME T-0018 lattice primitives the PDP uses (isNarrowerOrEqual/isEffective) composed in one coversInvoke helper. request durably inserts a row into a new tenant-isolated table choros.invoke_proposal (migration 043, status='proposed') and emits invoke.request; command emits invoke.command and returns 202 {invocation_id} with dispatch as a day-1 no-op stub. Both audit writes go through the single canonical appendAuditEvent seam (T-0031/T-0068) via a new pure encoder encodeInvokeAuditEvent mirroring encodeGrantAuditEvent. All shared-file changes are strictly additive: no edits to grant-lattice.ts, grant-resolver.ts, grants.ts, or router.ts logic.

rejected_alternatives.option: Edit the ResourceType union in grant-lattice.ts to add 'agent' (or thread an 'agent' kind through ObjectHandle and route through resolveFor).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: grant-lattice.ts and object-handle.ts are frozen seams under the additive-only sister contract. Editing the union risks the 122-test count regression (AC-13) and resolveFor's frozen signature (AC-14). The DB column is plain TEXT and the existing widening cast (resourceType as Grant['resourceType']) already used in grants.ts covers 'agent' transparently; the invoke covering-check keys on operation, not resource_type.

rejected_alternatives.option: Thread a synthetic record-shaped ObjectHandle for the target agent through resolveFor(.., 'invoke') to satisfy NF-2 literally.
rejected_alternatives.why_not: ObjectHandle has no agent kind (only application/registry/record) and its signature is frozen (AC-14). Forcing an agent target into a record handle is a lie that would either corrupt the record-resolution path or require editing the frozen seam. We satisfy NF-2's INTENT (no second decision path, reuse the T-0018 algebra) by composing the same exported lattice primitives the PDP itself uses, in one isolated coversInvoke helper.

rejected_alternatives.option: Declare FK from invoke_proposal.caller_id/target_id to choros.employee(tenant_id,id).
rejected_alternatives.why_not: T-0017 FK-lesson: cross-table FKs that may not exist in bare/partial schema sequences cause BUILD bounces. effect_resource (022) set the precedent of a self-contained PK with logical references validated in the app layer; invoke_proposal follows it. target_id is validated against agent_card at the HTTP boundary (FR-8) regardless.

rejected_alternatives.option: Write a local invoke-audit writer (separate INSERT into audit_event) for speed.
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Violates NF-3 and the T-0031 one-preimage-rule lesson: two preimage rules on the same vocab-pinned audit_event/audit_head tables make a verifier false-positive tamper and break density verification on a mixed chain. Invoke audit MUST go through appendAuditEvent (the same sink grant/lifecycle audit uses).

contracts: POST /api/invoke/request  body:{target_agent_id:uuid, goal:string, context?:object} → 400 VALIDATION (target not agent_card/kind!='agent'/bad body) | 403 FORBIDDEN (no covering invoke-grant; no row, no audit) | 201 Created {id} + invoke_proposal(status='proposed') + 'invoke.request' audit (INSERT+audit in one withTenantTx).
POST /api/invoke/command  body:{target_agent_id:uuid, goal:string, context?:object} → 400 | 403 (as above) | 202 Accepted {invocation_id:uuid} + 'invoke.command' audit; dispatch = no-op stub.

coversInvoke(grant, target, now, oracle): boolean = grant.operation==='invoke' && isEffective(grant, now) && grant.resourceFacet.agent_role_id === target.roleId && isNarrowerOrEqual(target.orgScope, grant.scope, oracle). Composes ONLY T-0018 exports; owns no new lattice math.

encodeInvokeAuditEvent(e: InvokeAuditEvent, nowMs: number, idOverride?: string): AuditEventInput — pure, IO-free; type=e.kind, actor=e.actor, subject=e.targetAgentId, scope=e.orgScope, via=null, proposed_by=null, confirmed_by=null, payload={mode,target_agent_id,agent_role_id,org_scope,goal}.

resolveFor signature UNCHANGED (AC-14): resolveFor(deps, handle, subject, op, invokeCtx?, guardCtx?) — T-0024 adds NO parameter and routes the agent-target decision through coversInvoke (composed PDP primitives), not through a record-shaped handle.

Grant create/revoke (FR-6): existing POST /api/grants {operation:'invoke',resource_type:'agent',resource_facet:{agent_role_id}} and POST /api/grants/:id/revoke — ZERO new grant-API code; existing handlers accept the new TEXT values and emit grant.create/grant.revoke.
Route wiring: src/http/invoke.ts exports registerInvokeRoutes(router, pool); wired in server.ts under the existing if(grantsPool) block — additive, no edit to existing registrations.
